strategy.title: No plan: expedited deposition transcripts settle after the deadline
strategy.why: The only opening has four written acceptances at $1,800 ($7,200 gross, $900 direct cost each, $0 exposure), but its evidenced time to first cash is 60 days, so none of that cash settles inside the 14-day window.

alternatives.title: Run the transcript deals anyway on a 60-day horizon
alternatives.why: Economics are positive ($900 margin per deal) and four buyers agreed, but cash lands on day ~60, after the 14-day deadline; only works if the deadline moves.

sources.claim: Time to first cash is 60 days
sources.population: Litigation firms buying expedited deposition transcripts

sources.claim: Direct costs $900 per job (Verbatim Reporting Group quote)

noPlan.decisiveGap: SETTLES_IN_TIME: the only opening's cash arrives 60 days after the work starts, beyond the 14-day window, so $0 of the $6,000 settles in time.
noPlan.resolution: Move the deadline to at least 60 days (the four agreed $1,800 deals then cover $7,200), or find an opening that pays on or before delivery, e.g. negotiate upfront/at-delivery payment terms with the agreed litigation firms.

excluded.why: Cash settles at 60 days, after the 14-day deadline.

constraints.suggestion: Extend the window to at least 60 days so the agreed transcript deals settle.
